## Acceptance cases

### safe_bumps

### progressive_hits

### quantity_and_thickness

Capacity scales with represented volume, so twice the plate takes about twice the hits. Doubling the represented thickness doubles the load-bearing area and halves the stress, so a hit that dents the thin plate stays recoverable on the thick one.

### wood_vs_armor

### resting_support

A safe resting load charges nothing however long it rests. An overload yields and charges plateau work each tick until the plank fails in bounded time, sooner for a larger overload; a host-measured plastic displacement replaces the fallback progression.

### beam_connections

Three wood connections along a cantilever under one tip load. Only the root connection exceeds its bending strength; it fails after a bounded number of ticks while the other two keep their full integrity and the assembly is not deleted.

### partition

Splitting one contact into equivalent colliders must not multiply energy. Merged sub-contacts reproduce the single contact exactly; charging each part with the whole event would overstate the damage several times over.

### fixed_step

The plank press and a connection moment just past their safe limits, stepped at 30, 60, 120 and 240 Hz, where 240 Hz is the 60 Hz tick with four substeps. The fallback is integrated exactly over each call, so the work consumed and the integrity after 1/30 s, in column a, match at every rate, and each failure lands within one tick of the continuous failure time. The other columns describe the tick that ends at 1/30 s, which shrinks as the rate rises.
